ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

rockwood — pattern 3

A patient has a visibly elevated distal clavicle after shoulder trauma. Both AC and coracoclavicular ligaments are completely torn. The coracoclavicular distance is approximately 60% greater than on the other side, without posterior or inferior clavicular displacement. Which Rockwood acromioclavicular injury type best fits this pattern?

  1. Type I
  2. Type III
  3. Type IV
  4. Type V
  5. Type VI
Answer and explanation

Type III

Type III: Complete AC and CC ligament disruption with superior displacement and a coracoclavicular distance increase of about 25–100%.

Option explanations

Type III: Type III: Complete AC and CC ligament disruption with superior displacement and a coracoclavicular distance increase of about 25–100%.

Type IV: Type IV describes posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius. The case instead matches Type III.

Type V: Type V describes marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%. The case instead matches Type III.

Type VI: Type VI describes inferior displacement of the distal clavicle, beneath the acromion or coracoid. The case instead matches Type III.

Type I: Type I describes an AC ligament sprain with intact coracoclavicular ligaments and no radiographic displacement. The case instead matches Type III.
